description: Laser SDK: agent memory, durable workflows, sessions and messaging on Apache Iggy, with matching Rust, Python and TypeScript clients.
rules: Never print or log the connection string or its password. Read it from LASER_CONNECTION_STRING inside the program.

Connect with Laser.connect_env() in Python, Laser.connectEnv() in TypeScript or Laser::connect_env() in Rust, which read the connection string from LASER_CONNECTION_STRING. A LaserData API key is not a connection string: copy the connection string from the deployment's Credentials tab in the Console.
Python installs with pip install laser-sdk and imports laser_sdk. TypeScript installs @laserdata/laser-sdk. Rust adds laser-sdk with the agent and kv features, plus tokio, serde and serde_json.

Start from the two complete programs at the top of each README: a three-step workflow of in-process steps that prints its outcome as JSON (step(label, run=...) in Python, stepLocal(label, run) in TypeScript, step_local(label, run) in Rust), and a memory correction for one user with memory.supersede(old_id, new_fact) followed by a recall that prints the current facts. The examples folder holds them as workflow and memory-correction (workflow.py and memory_correction.py in Python).

Work in a scratch stream and clean it up at the end: async with laser.scratch_stream(prefix) as scratch in Python, await using scratch = await laser.scratchStream(prefix) in TypeScript, laser.scratch_stream(prefix) then scratch.delete() in Rust. To keep what the program writes, use a named stream instead, through LASER_STREAM or with_default_stream(name).

A workflow run and the first memory write create their stream and topics, so they need no bootstrap call. Correct a remembered fact with supersede, which forgets the old fact in every conversation. A default recall reads the writes the same connection made.
Use the SDK's own workflow, memory and session APIs for durable results. A local list, dict or plain function is not durable.
A LaserData Cloud deployment admits a Laser SDK connection only from an address its access rules allow over TCP.
